problem.title: One Cut Through the Corner
problem.statement: An L-shaped region can be split without overlap into a 6-by-4 rectangle and a 5-by-2 rectangle. What is its area?
hints: The two rectangles have disjoint interiors.

validationMethods: independent unit-square total 24+10 and option audit

problem.title: Area of a Frame
problem.statement: A rectangular frame has outer dimensions 12 by 8 and a rectangular opening 6 by 4. What is the area of the frame?

solutionSteps.title: Find whole and hole
solutionSteps.body: The outer area is 96 and the opening is 24.

validationMethods: independent partition check: frame plus opening 72+24=96; option audit

problem.title: Count the Shared Square Once
problem.statement: A 6-by-4 rectangle and a 5-by-3 rectangle overlap in a 2-by-2 square. What is the area of their union?
hints: The overlap has then been counted twice.

solutionSteps.title: Remove duplicate coverage
solutionSteps.body: Subtract one copy of the 2 × 2 overlap: 39 − 4 = 35.

validationMethods: independent exclusive-piece audit: 20 outside first-only plus 11 second-only plus 4 shared equals 35; options audited

problem.title: Can the Areas Be Claimed Equal?
problem.statement: Two quadrilateral pieces look congruent in a sketch marked not to scale, but no lengths, angle marks, or transformation relationship are given. What can be concluded about their areas?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Their equality cannot be determined from the given information.

hints: Appearance in a not-to-scale drawing is not a measurement.
Look for exact evidence of congruence.

solutionSteps.title: Audit the evidence
solutionSteps.body: No dimensions, congruence marks, or rigid motion connects the pieces.

solutionSteps.title: Conclude
solutionSteps.body: They may have equal or unequal areas, so equality cannot be determined.

validationMethods: logical givens audit finds no area-determining relation
counterexample method: sketches with same appearance can be assigned different dimensions, so only choice D is guaranteed

problem.title: Half by a Diagonal
problem.statement: A 10-by-7 rectangle is cut along a diagonal. What is the area of either triangular piece?
hints: The diagonal creates two congruent triangles.
Find the rectangle's area and halve it.

solutionSteps.title: Use congruent halves
solutionSteps.body: The diagonal triangles match under a half-turn, so each area is 70 ÷ 2 = 35.

validationMethods: independent triangle formula using base 10 and height 7 gives 35; option audit
